title: cputime
summary: Return total CPU time used by the current RunMat process.

gpu_support.notes: Host-side process timing helper. GPU providers are never consulted.

description: `cputime` returns the total CPU time used by the current RunMat process in seconds. It is intended for legacy MATLAB compatibility; prefer `timeit` or `tic`/`toc` for wall-clock benchmarking.
behaviors: Returns a finite, nonnegative scalar double in seconds.
Native Unix builds use host process CPU accounting via getrusage.
Native Windows builds use host process CPU accounting via GetProcessTimes.

WASM/browser builds do not expose process CPU accounting, so RunMat returns monotonic seconds since the WASM runtime first used `cputime`; differences remain useful for compatibility code, but the measurement is wall-clock elapsed time rather than true CPU time.
GPU providers are never consulted, and the builtin is excluded from fusion plans.

examples.description: Measure CPU Time Used By Code

faqs.question: How is `cputime` different from `tic` and `toc`?
faqs.answer: `cputime` measures CPU time consumed by the process on native targets. `tic`/`toc` measure wall-clock elapsed time.

faqs.question: Why does WASM use a wall-clock fallback?
faqs.answer: Browsers do not expose process CPU time. RunMat keeps the no-argument scalar API available so MATLAB compatibility code that subtracts two calls still runs.

faqs.question: Does `cputime` reset?
faqs.answer: No. Like MATLAB, native builds return total CPU time since the current process started. On WASM, the wall-clock fallback is measured from the first `cputime` call. To measure a section of code, subtract two readings.

points: `t` is a scalar double value in seconds.
Use `cputime` differences to measure CPU time spent between two points.
